children: Australia building approvals for new homes fell by 3.6% in July 2026, led by a 4.5% fall in private house approvals, as the fallout from higher interest rates and tax increases on property investors continues to be felt, the Housing Industry Association's senior economist, Tom Devitt says. New home building activity had good momentum heading into 2026, but higher rates, tax changes, global conflict and surging fuel costs, has interrupted the expansion, he adds. The headwinds appear set to reduce the supply of new homes, and lead to a worsening in affordability, he adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
